gotchas_discovered.gotcha: Small Dataset Sequential Scans Are Optimal
gotchas_discovered.description: Current dataset has only 0-5 rows in most tables, making sequential scans more efficient than index usage
gotchas_discovered.impact: Previous attempts failed because they expected to see index usage in EXPLAIN ANALYZE output
gotchas_discovered.solution: Documented that this is expected behavior and indexes will activate when data grows

gotchas_discovered.description: Reading an index + fetching rows costs more than scanning 5 rows sequentially
gotchas_discovered.impact: PostgreSQL optimizer correctly chooses sequential scan despite indexes being present
gotchas_discovered.solution: Provided performance projection table showing thresholds when indexes become beneficial (100+ rows)

gotchas_discovered.gotcha: Testing Index Functionality Without Large Dataset
gotchas_discovered.description: Cannot demonstrate index performance improvements on current small dataset
gotchas_discovered.impact: Previous approaches tried to explain why indexes aren't used, causing confusion
gotchas_discovered.solution: Implemented forced index testing (enable_seqscan=OFF) to prove indexes work without needing large dataset

gotchas_discovered.description: Query plans can vary based on current data, statistics, and table size
gotchas_discovered.impact: Single EXPLAIN ANALYZE run may not show index usage even if indexes are functional
gotchas_discovered.solution: Created repeatable verification scripts that can be run multiple times as data grows

gotchas_discovered.gotcha: Django Dependencies vs Direct SQL Testing
gotchas_discovered.description: Some environments may not have Django running or virtual environment active
gotchas_discovered.impact: Previous Python-only approaches couldn't be executed in all contexts
gotchas_discovered.solution: Provided both SQL (no dependencies) and Python (Django integration) verification paths
